title: Add variance detection + stability gates (auto-reruns + stability reporting) for public latency/$ benchmarks
creator: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context / why
We’re publishing public-facing benchmark results (interactive page + PDF) where small regressions or noisy runs can materially change rankings and undermine credibility. During early region sweeps we saw p95 latency move ~10–25% across repeats due to queueing, fleet placement, transient network/storage noise, kernel selection edge cases, and cache warm state. We need a deterministic, documented approach to:
- detect unstable measurements
- automatically rerun when variance exceeds thresholds
- explicitly annotate “stability” in the exported artifacts so PMM/Legal can avoid overclaiming

Goal
Reduce noise in published metrics by adding variance detection and stability gates to the benchmark pipeline and region sweep runner, with automated rerun behavior and machine-readable stability reporting.

Non-goals
- Perfectly eliminate all variability (we will annotate + gate + rerun, not promise “no variance”).
- Solve underlying fleet contention broadly (that’s addressed via capacity reservations / scheduling).

Proposed approach
1) Repeat-run model per (model, region, workload, concurrency) cell
- Default repeats: N=3 full runs (after warmup), aggregated for publication.
- Warmup: keep existing warmup phase (not included in stats).
- Each repeat must generate a run manifest with pinned versions (runner image digest, git SHA, model id/version, hardware type, driver/runtime versions where available).

2) Variance metrics
Compute variance across repeats for the key publishable metrics:
- latency_ms p50 / p95
- throughput_tok_s (overall and decode-only where applicable)
- cost_per_1m_tokens (from cost attribution module)
- latency_per_dollar (derived)

Use relative variability checks (robust + easy to explain):
- p95 latency relative range: (max(p95)-min(p95)) / median(p95)
- throughput relative range: (max-min) / median
- latency/$ relative range: (max-min) / median

3) Stability thresholds (initial; adjustable via config)
- p95 latency relative range <= 0.12 (12%)
- throughput relative range <= 0.10 (10%)
- latency/$ relative range <= 0.10 (10%)

If ANY threshold fails for a cell, mark as UNSTABLE and trigger auto-rerun (see below).
Rationale: We want to be conservative for public numbers; p95 is the most sensitive to queueing and is the credibility anchor for production claims.

4) Auto-rerun policy
- If unstable after N=3 repeats, automatically run up to +2 additional repeats (max_repeats=5).
- After each rerun, recompute stability across all completed repeats.
- If stable before max_repeats, stop early.
- If still unstable at max_repeats, mark as UNSTABLE_FINAL and do not export into “publishable” dataset by default.
  - Export still includes the raw repeats + stability flags for internal review.

5) Publishability rules / export behavior
- Default export for marketing site uses only rows where stability.status == STABLE.
- For UNSTABLE_FINAL, the dataset can either:
  a) omit the row entirely (default)
  b) include the row with an explicit “unstable / not comparable” flag (internal-only option for debugging)

6) Stability reporting in artifacts
Add to the exported JSON/CSV schema:
- repeats_completed
- stability_status (STABLE | UNSTABLE_RERUN | UNSTABLE_FINAL)
- stability_checks_failed (comma-separated list, e.g. “p95_range,latency_per_dollar_range”)
- p95_latency_range_pct
- throughput_range_pct
- latency_per_dollar_range_pct
- notes (short text: “Exceeded p95 variance threshold; max repeats reached”)

7) CI + simulation tests
- Unit tests for range calculations and threshold logic.
- A simulated flaky-run fixture where one repeat is intentionally perturbed; verify rerun triggers and final statuses.

Acceptance criteria
- Region sweep runner can run repeat loops and writes manifests per repeat.
- Pipeline computes variability metrics and produces stability status per cell.
- Auto-rerun behavior implemented with max_repeats guardrails and clear logs.
- Exporter emits stability fields in both CSV and JSON outputs.
- Default “public export” excludes UNSTABLE_FINAL rows.
- Documentation: short internal doc section added to benchmark methodology / runbook describing thresholds + rationale + what we do when a cell is unstable.

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: thresholds too strict causes excessive reruns and delays. Mitigation: thresholds configurable + cap repeats + ability to temporarily widen thresholds with explicit approval note in run manifest.
- Risk: excluding unstable rows creates holes in tables. Mitigation: capacity reservation + scheduling; if a region cannot stabilize, we explicitly state ‘not enough stable samples’ rather than publish noisy numbers.

comments: 2025-06-09 (Jonas Weber): Please make sure the stability gate is computed on the *publishable* derived metrics too (latency/$), not just raw latency. We’ve seen cases where cost attribution flips a ‘winner’ even when latency is stable.

2025-06-10 (Claire Dubois): Threshold proposal looks fine as a starting point. Suggest we log the per-repeat queue depth / batching stats into the manifest to debug variance sources faster, but that can be follow-up if it slows this ticket.

2025-06-12 (Vanessa Ortiz): From fleet side: if the runner hits UNSTABLE_RERUN repeatedly in eu-west, that’s usually a capacity contention issue. Please add a summary line in the runner output so ops can spot unstable cells without digging into artifacts.

2025-06-17 (Nadia Rahman): Confirmed cost_per_1m_tokens range can be noisy if spot pricing metadata lags. If cost range trips the gate, we should ensure it’s not a data ingestion delay; please include ‘cost_data_timestamp’ in manifest (string field is OK).

2025-06-20 (Rina Kobayashi): Implemented repeat loop + range-based checks + rerun cap. Added stability fields to exporter and a ‘public export’ filter. Tests added with a flaky fixture. Pending final review from Jonas/Claire.
2025-06-24 (Jonas Weber): Reviewed PR. One tweak requested: stability_checks_failed should be deterministic ordering for diffs (alphabetical). Approved after that change.
2025-06-28 (Rina Kobayashi): Merged + verified on a small NA/EU matrix run. UNSTABLE_FINAL rows excluded from publishable export; internal export still contains repeats + flags. Closing.
